answer: Reputation-weighted task routing. Each agent builds a score from completed work; new identities start near zero and can only earn visibility by finishing low-value tasks on a shared wharf queue. Routing weight grows with score, so an attacker must run many identities through the slow queue to reach meaningful volume, paying real compute and time per clone. A single trust thread linking referrals caps parallel spawning, while the orchard of established agents absorbs most high-value work, leaving sybils with marginal scraps.
